name: Kegel
summary: A targeted pelvic floor isometric exercise focused on lifting and contracting the deep pelvic musculature while keeping surrounding muscles relaxed.

setup: Lie on your back on an exercise mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Rest your arms comfortably at your sides and ensure your abdominal, gluteal, and thigh muscles are fully relaxed.
steps: Exhale softly and draw the pelvic floor muscles inward and upward, as if trying to stop the flow of urine or hold back gas.
Hold the contraction steadily at the top without tensing your glutes or holding your breath.
Gently release the tension and allow the pelvic floor to fully relax before initiating the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and smoothly throughout the exercise, never holding your breath during the squeeze.

common_faults.fault: Bearing down or pushing outward instead of pulling upward.
common_faults.correction: Focus on an inward lifting sensation toward your navel rather than straining downward.

common_faults.fault: Co-contracting the gluteus maximus or adductors.
common_faults.correction: Place your hands lightly on your buttocks or inner thighs to verify that they remain completely relaxed throughout the contraction.

common_faults.fault: Holding breath to brace the abdomen.
common_faults.correction: Count your hold seconds out loud to force consistent breathing.

precautions: Do not routinely perform this exercise while actively urinating, as this can interfere with normal bladder function.
